subject.title: Santa Maria — Measure C2026 (City Of Santa Maria General Services)

positions.statement: "Measure C ✓ Vote Yes" — "City of Santa Maria: increases the local sales tax rate from 8.75% to 9.25% to fund community facilities, parks, the library, and street repairs."

subject.title: Allan Hancock Joint Community College District — Measure H (Affordable Higher Education Bond)

positions.statement: "Measure H ✓ Vote Yes" — "Allan Hancock Joint Community College District: authorizes up to $290 million in bonds to repair, upgrade, and modernize college facilities across the district."

subject.title: Santa Ynez Valley Union High School District — Measure D2026 (Santa Ynez Valley Union High School Quality Education/Career Training Measure)

positions.statement: "Measure D ✓ Vote Yes" — "Santa Ynez Valley Union High School District: authorizes an $80 million bond for campus facilities improvements."

subject.title: Isla Vista Community Services District — Measure E2026 (Increased Isla Vista Municipal Infrastructure and Services)

positions.statement: "Measure E ✓ Vote Yes" — "Isla Vista Community Services District: adds a utility tax to fund weekend safety response, resident parking, and better street lighting."

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: "Prop 1 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Authorizes $11.25 billion in state bonds for affordable housing and veterans' home loans."

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: "Prop 2 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Raises the cap on the state's rainy day fund and changes budget reserve rules."

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: "Prop 3 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Makes permanent the existing tax rates on millionaires, funding K-12 schools and community colleges."

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: "Prop 4 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Allows public financing of political campaigns for candidates who agree to spending limits."

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: "Prop 5 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Eliminates the simultaneous successor election in a recall, leaving the office vacant until filled by law."

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: "Prop 37 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Authorizes up to $25 billion in bonds to create low-cost, state-backed mortgages for middle-income home buyers."

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: "Prop 38 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Authorizes $8.4 billion in state bonds for immunology and immunotherapy research."

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: "Prop 39 ✕ Vote No" — "Imposes new voter ID and citizenship-verification requirements that make it harder for eligible Californians to register and vote."

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: "Prop 40 ✓ Vote Yes" — "Imposes a one-time 5% tax on individuals and trusts with covered assets over $1 billion, funding health care and food assistance."

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: "Prop 41 ✕ Vote No" — "Creates new audit mandates and locks in permanent restrictions on future state special taxes, tying lawmakers' hands on emergency revenue."

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: "Prop 42 ✕ Vote No" — "Blocks the state from ever taxing personal property or wealth, including stocks and investment accounts, shielding the richest Californians' assets."

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: "Prop 43 ✕ Vote No" — "Makes it harder for local communities to fund schools, transit, and services by requiring a two-thirds vote for local special taxes, even those proposed directly by voters."

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: "Prop 44 ✕ Vote No" — "Imposes rigid spending mandates and penalties on community health clinics serving low-income patients, threatening their ability to operate."

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: "Prop 45 ✕ Vote No" — "Guts environmental review and limits the public's ability to legally challenge harmful development projects, weakening CEQA protections."
